Build a Reproducibility Bundle

Source: R/mkbndl.R
mkbndl.Rd

Packs a project folder into one zip that anyone can unzip and run with a double-click: START_HERE.command on macOS, START_HERE.bat on Windows, start_here.sh on Linux. The launchers find R, the runner (setup_and_run.R) checks the packages the project lists, finds or downloads the data (checking it against the pinned SHA-256), or generates synthetic data from the project's recipe, runs the project's analysis script and summarises its manifest.json in plain language.

Usage

mkbndl(project, dest, data = NULL, version = "1", overwrite = FALSE)

Arguments

project

A project folder, or the name of an example shipped with the package ("otis-mrp", the Ontario restrictive confinement analysis).

dest

An existing folder to write the zip into.

data

Optional path to the data file, copied into the bundle (under the file name the provenance pins) so it runs offline. NULL (default) leaves it out: the runner asks for it, offers to download it, or uses synthetic data.

version

Version label in the zip's name, default "1".

overwrite

Replace a zip of the same name, default FALSE.

Value

An object of class rmbl_bundle: a list with path (the zip), sha256, bytes, files (the paths inside the zip), project (the project name) and data (whether the data file is inside). It prints as a box.

Details

A project is a folder holding at least config.json and the analysis script it names (default analysis.R); mkbndlproj() writes a working starter. data_provenance.json pins the data file (name, URL, SHA-256, licence) and may carry a schema$synthetic_recipe for the offline synthetic route. Every other file in the folder is copied into the bundle too, except hidden files, results_* folders and zip files.

The runner calls the analysis script as Rscript analysis.R <data file> <results folder>, with BRICKLAYER_SYNTHETIC=1 set on synthetic data. The script writes manifest.json into the results folder: mkmnf(), recrd() and wrmnfjs() build it, and they are in the bundle (the script sources them from its own folder, as the starter does), so the reviewer needs only R and the packages listed in r_packages. To call other functions of this package from the analysis, list "rmoriebricklayer" in r_packages.

Optional keys of config.json: project (name, title, paper_title, work_type, author, contact, orcid, affiliation, supervisor, licence), analysis$r_script, r_packages, env_packages (packages needed only when an environment variable is set), optional_stages (opt-in stages with their own packages), synthetic_env (another variable that turns on the synthetic route), data$default_candidates, network$endpoints, summary$what_was_done and expected (total_checks, pass_real).

Before zipping, every internal name the bundled R files call is checked to be defined by a bundled file, and by one the runner itself sources when the runner calls it: a bundle that would stop with “could not find function” on the reviewer's machine is refused here instead.

Nothing is written except the zip in dest; the staging folder is a temporary directory removed on exit. Send the SHA-256 that is printed to recipients separately, so they can check the zip was not altered.

Errors: project that is neither a folder nor a bundled example; a project without config.json or without its analysis script; a project file whose name a bundle file already uses; dest that is not an existing folder; a zip that exists when overwrite is FALSE; data that is not an existing file; a version with characters other than letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore.

See also

mkbndlproj() for a starter project; mkmnf() and recrd() for the manifest the analysis writes.

Examples

# a starter project, bundled
proj <- file.path(tempdir(), "demo-project")
mkbndlproj(proj, title = "Demo analysis", author = "A. Researcher")
#> ╭── Bundle project ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Folder  /tmp/RtmpysAncb/demo-project                                      │
#> │   Files   config.json, data_provenance.json, analysis.R                     │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   Edit config.json (who and what), data_provenance.json (the data file,     │
#> │   its URL and SHA-256) and analysis.R (the checks), then build the zip      │
#> │   with mkbndl().                                                            │
#> │   It runs as it is on synthetic data, so the bundle can be tried before     │
#> │   the analysis is written.                                                  │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
b <- mkbndl(proj, dest = tempdir(), overwrite = TRUE)
b
#> ╭── Reproducibility bundle ───────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Project    demo-project                                                   │
#> │   Zip        demo-project_v1.zip                                            │
#> │   Folder     /tmp/RtmpysAncb                                                │
#> │   Size       197.2 KB                                                       │
#> │   Files      26                                                             │
#> │   Data file  not inside                                                     │
#> │   SHA-256    771200dacacd340741c8f765e266494b56d422c5f39ae2db3ad8c039e1648b │
#> │              0d                                                             │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   Recipients unzip it and double-click START_HERE.command (macOS) or        │
#> │   START_HERE.bat (Windows), or run ./start_here.sh (Linux).                 │
#> │   The data file is not inside: the runner finds it, downloads it and        │
#> │   checks its SHA-256, or runs on synthetic data.                            │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   Send the SHA-256 separately from the zip, so recipients can check the     │
#> │   copy they received was not altered.                                       │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
head(b$files)
#> [1] "demo-project_v1/"                   "demo-project_v1/INSTRUCTIONS.txt"  
#> [3] "demo-project_v1/README.md"          "demo-project_v1/SECURITY.md"       
#> [5] "demo-project_v1/START_HERE.bat"     "demo-project_v1/START_HERE.command"

# the example shipped with the package
otis <- mkbndl("otis-mrp", dest = tempdir(), overwrite = TRUE)
otis$sha256
#> [1] "358171eb5d6c703156aa3e3711e056281a48b92aa467ea60c1a01ee5f571c8c1"

# an existing zip is kept unless overwrite = TRUE
try(mkbndl(proj, dest = tempdir()))
#> Error : /tmp/RtmpysAncb/demo-project_v1.zip exists: pass overwrite = TRUE to replace it
